It is the binding cybersecurity standard for nearly all U.S. providers and their BAs and OCR's primary enforcement basis. Its required risk analysis (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)) anchors any gap assessment. 42 U.S.C. 17941 rewards 12 months of recognized security practices. Map to HPH CPGs/405(d) HICP and watch the Jan 2025 NPRM, which would make most controls mandatory.

Protected Health Information / ePHI (HIPAA); SUD treatment records (42 CFR Part 2); PHR / consumer health app data (FTC HBNR); Payment card and patient financial/billing data; Medicaid applicant/beneficiary data (42 CFR 431.300); Genomic, reproductive and behavioral health data (heightened state protections); Medical device telemetry; Child care and family services case files (state law / program rules)

HHS is the SRMA for the HPH Sector (see c-hph). Voluntary baselines: HHS 405(d) HICP and HPH CPGs. All 50 states, DC and the territories have breach notification statutes with differing triggers, deadlines and regulator-notice duties. They are not enumerated here.
